g0.rationale: Section 2.2 five-step test. Step 1: directions located (aggregated Rossmann copy, packet confidence moderate). Step 2: three stated modes. (a) 'Intensivpflege - ins nasse Haar einmassieren, 3-5 Minuten einwirken lassen, mit warmem Wasser ausspuelen': stated contact time and rinse -> QUALIFIES. (b) 'Fuer leichtes Kaemmen - ins handtuchtrockene Haar verteilen, nicht ausspuelen': leave-in, not rinsed -> fails. (c) 'Zum Baendigen - ins trockene Haar verteilen, nicht ausspuelen': leave-in on dry hair -> fails. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies -> classify that mode only, multi_use = true, uncovered modes named. Charter F1 names Isana 3in1 among the live multi-use boundary cases resolved as eligible mode-scoped.
evidenceSignals: multi_use: true
multi_use_covered_mode: post_shampoo_rinse_out_mask
multi_use_uncovered_modes: [leave_in_towel_dry_detangling, leave_in_dry_hair_taming]
multi_use_directions_source: packet directions block, aggregated Rossmann retailer copy (confidence moderate - a documented sourcing gap on the directions leg of section 2.3)
The 3-5 minute contact time is protocol metadata with zero classification credit
Placement 'nasses Haar' with no root exclusion stated; not an explicit whole-head/root instruction, so no P5 deviation is recorded

tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved, no anomaly, and the longest above-tail segment in the set (fifteen entries). ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL (14) and CITRIC ACID (15) precede it; neither is a tail-class marker - Citric Acid is explicitly barred from being one (section 3.1), and Isopropyl Alcohol is a silicone/fragrance carrier with no care meaning (lexicon family 2). Consequence: essentially the whole payload of this formula, including two protein species and a cocoa butter, is above the tail and genuinely material.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment (ranks 1-15) of the exact-market INCI; formula-only structural position.
conditioningLevel.rationale: All three section 9.1 structural signals are satisfied on a long above-tail segment, with lipid breadth well beyond the threshold. E2 ceiling: architecture, not delivered conditioning.
evidenceSignals: S1 satisfied: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (5) and STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (13) - two distinct species (a permanent quat and a protonatable amidoamine) above the tail
S2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2
S3 satisfied six-fold: DICAPRYLYL ETHER (3), COCOCAPRYLATE (4), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7), PRUNUS AMYGDALUS DULCIS OIL (8), HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL (9), THEOBROMA CACAO SEED BUTTER (12)
Not counted toward S1: LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (10) is a quaternised protein (R5 family), not a cationic surfactant
CITRIC ACID (15) read as the amidoamine neutraliser context (lexicon C3), not as an active
conditioningLevel.derivation: Section 9.1 S1/S2/S3 counting on the above-tail slice; 3 of 3 -> high.
thresholdReasoning: Why high, not moderate: three independent signals against a >= 2 threshold, with S3 exceeded threefold.
Why high, not low: every leg of the low anchor is falsified.
TOCOPHEROL (23) was checked and excluded: it is an oil-phase antioxidant protecting the formula, not a care payload (lexicon 5c), and it is tail-side.
counterSignals: None of the section 9.1 named counter-signals is present in force: no rheology-only thickener at all, and the payload is above the tail rather than in a hero tail
The list is moderate in length (23 entries), so the count-is-not-payload caution has little purchase here
limitations: Section 9.1's honest limitation on the three-step scale applies; this product sits comfortably inside high rather than near a boundary.

weightPotential.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment (ranks 1-15); ingredient-informed matching prior, not a prediction of visible flattening.
weightPotential.rationale: The required rich base holds and two independent R4b heavy lipids sit above the tail. E2 ceiling. Confidence is held at moderate because the product's own directions describe two leave-in modes, which sits awkwardly against a weight-high architecture.
evidenceSignals: Required base leg 1: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (5) and STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (13) - two distinct cationics above the tail
Required base leg 2: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2
Supporting alternative (a): COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7), named in the standard's R4b heavy-triglyceride list, and THEOBROMA CACAO SEED BUTTER (12), a butter
Supporting alternative (b) absent: no silicone anywhere in the list
weightPotential.derivation: Section 9.2 ruled anchors: base plus at least one alternative -> high.
thresholdReasoning: Why high, not moderate: base and alternative (a) both hold, on two independent heavy species, both well above the tail. The moderate residual applies only when the base or every alternative fails.
Why high, not low: all three legs of the low anchor are falsified.

The section 9.2 conflict fallback was considered and deliberately NOT applied. Its trigger is an exact-product intended finish that materially contradicts the anchor (a 'leichte Pflege' or 'ohne zu beschweren' positioning). What I have instead is a directions fact - two leave-in modes on towel-dry and dry hair. G2 forbids protocol metadata from crossing into a comparison property, so I did not let the directions move the value; I recorded the tension as a counter-signal and capped confidence.
counterSignals: The same product is directed to be left in on dry hair (mode c), which is hard to reconcile with a category-high weight architecture - recorded, not used as an input
No silicone: silicone-free proves nothing about lightness
'Mandelmilch' positioning suggests lightness on a naive read; a name is not weight evidence
limitations: The value stands on the written anchor, but the leave-in modes are a genuine external signal that the finished product is not experienced as heavy. Only exact-product finished evidence (section 8 body/lightness method) could resolve this, and none exists.
Listed in uncertain_fields for that reason.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment; comparative emphasis only, never a user-state assertion (G6).
careDirection.rationale: A material R5 protein-film route is established twice over above the tail, and the balanced test's S3 leg is satisfied by a genuinely substantial six-species lipid stack. This is balanced in the substantive sense section 9.3 reserves it for. E2 ceiling.
evidenceSignals: Qualifying R5 species 1: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN (6) - a hydrolyzed protein above the tail, and within the first eight above-tail ranks, so leg (b) of the material-R5 test is satisfied on its own

Qualifying R5 species 2: LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (10) - a cationised (quaternised) protein derivative, explicitly a qualifying R5 class with higher substantivity; leg (a) is therefore also satisfied

Balanced second leg: S3 satisfied by six distinct lipids above the tail (3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 12) - here 'substantial R4 lipid/emollient stack' is met in substance, not merely on the two-species breadth count
Humectant leg not needed and not satisfied: PANTHENOL (11) is the only R9 humectant above the tail; there is no glycerin in this formula at all
No free-amino-acid tokens are being miscounted as protein
careDirection.derivation: Section 9.3: material R5 route satisfied on both legs; balanced = material R5 AND (humectant cluster OR S3); S3 holds -> balanced.
thresholdReasoning: Why balanced, not protein: the balanced disjunction's S3 branch is satisfied, and unlike packet 04 it is satisfied substantively (six lipids including a butter and a heavy triglyceride), so the value is not resting on a thin breadth count.

Why balanced, not moisture: moisture is the residual when no material R5 route exists. Two qualifying species above the tail, one of them cationised and one within the first eight above-tail ranks, is a material route on either leg of the test.

Confidence capped at moderate because D4 fires: multiple distinct R5 species above the tail is a heavy protein payload, which caps care_direction confidence at moderate and fires protein_payload_review. The cap is binding regardless of how well-supported the value otherwise is.
counterSignals: protein_payload_counter_signal: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN (rank 6), LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (rank 10) - trace-level record only, never a field, never a verdict, never a value modifier, and none of the banned overload vocabulary is used
'Milchprotein & Mandel' naming aligns with the protein leg, which is a coincidence of positioning and architecture rather than evidence - claims are barred from care_direction
limitations: The lexicon does not name 'Hydrolyzed Milk Protein' verbatim in family 5a (it names Hydrolyzed Casein among others). I treated it as a plainly qualifying hydrolyzed protein.

Balanced bridge-matches downstream, so this value carries real cost if it is inflated. I am satisfied it is not inflated here - both legs are substantive - but it should be checked against the reference key.

repairSupportLevel.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment; comparative temporary damage-support route, never measured repair.
repairSupportLevel.rationale: A distinct temporary protein/keratin-class fibre-film route is present above the tail on the same qualifying test as care_direction, which is exactly the medium bar. No named bond chemistry exists, so high is unreachable. E2 ceiling; no efficacy is asserted.
evidenceSignals: Material R5 route: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN (6) plus LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (10), the latter a cationised derivative that deposits more substantively than a neutral hydrolysate
bond_route = none: no maleate, no gluconamide pair, no bond-positioned peptide anywhere in the list
Explicit non-upgraders present and excluded: PANTHENOL (11), the plant oils, TOCOPHEROL (23), CITRIC ACID (15)
repairSupportLevel.derivation: Section 9.4: high gated on bond_route != none (fails); medium gated on the section 9.3 material-R5 test (holds) -> medium.
thresholdReasoning: Why medium, not low: the material-R5 test is satisfied on both of its legs, so this is not the ordinary-conditioning-only case.

Why medium, not high: high is gated solely and deterministically on a named bond token above the tail. There is none, and no amount of protein reaches high (hydrolyzed protein alone is an explicit non-qualifier for high).
Mask delta 1 tested: this product is also conditioning_level high, and that alone would have been repair low. The medium comes from the protein route, not from the richness.
Confidence follows the section 9.3 protein-route confidence, which is capped at moderate by D4.
counterSignals: INCI discloses no molecular weight, so the hydrolysate cannot support a penetration, strength, or breakage-reduction claim - it supports 'a protein film route is present', nothing more
The 3-5 minute dwell carries zero credit
limitations: E2 ceiling binding; no exact-product damage endpoint exists for this product.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Above-tail architecture plus the section 9.5.2 hierarchy; no claims summary available.
primaryFocus.rationale: Step 3 tests repair first and this formula clears it: a distinct R5 protein/peptide film route above the tail, carried by two species one of which is cationised. E2 ceiling: a comparative route, never an efficacy statement.
evidenceSignals: Step 3 repair clears: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN (6) + LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (10), a coherent substantive-deposition protein cluster rather than one token
Step 3 curl_support fails: no distinctive slip route beyond the baseline two-cationic base; no cationic polymer at all; no curl positioning
Step 3 color_care fails: no candidate, no positioning
Step 3 lightness fails: weight_potential is high
Step 4 moisture fails: PANTHENOL (11) is the only humectant above the tail and there is no glycerin in the formula - cluster size 1 against a required 3
Step 5 shine fails: no silicone, no cationic polymer, high lipid load
Step 6 smoothing fails: no distinct silicone or substantive polymer; the beyond-baseline feature is emollient richness
Step 7 detangling fails: baseline slip
primaryFocus.derivation: Section 9.5.2 in order; step 3's repair leg clears and terminates the hierarchy. focus_care_verdict = repair_supported: two distinct species including a cationised derivative is a coherent substantive/deposition cluster, not merely one protein token.
thresholdReasoning: Why repair, not general: general is step 8 and is reachable only when nothing clears earlier. The repair route clears on the same test the standard uses for care_direction and repair_support_level, so declining it here would be inconsistent across three fields.
Why repair, not moisture: no humectant cluster exists (one member), and step 4 is tested after step 3 in any case.
Why repair, not smoothing: step 6's dry-surface conjunct fails - there is no film former in this formula, only lipids and cationics.
claim_role = not_applicable: no claims summary. The product name's 'Milchprotein' would have corroborated the repair route, but corroboration was not needed and could not have created it.
counterSignals: This is a nourishing almond-milk-positioned 3in1, and 'repair' as its research headline is driven purely by the protein-film route clearing step 3 first. Worth calibration attention: the hierarchy has no comparative test between a qualifying protein route and a dominant emollient architecture, and the vocabulary has no richness value for the latter to win with.
The R5 route says a film route is present; it says nothing about strength or breakage (MW is invisible on a label)
limitations: Confidence moderate: a reviewer who treats the two protein species as insufficiently 'distinct' (both are protein hydrolysates, one quaternised) would fall through to step 8 and land on general.

secondaryFocus.rationale: No further candidate clears its own threshold. E2 ceiling.
evidenceSignals: moisture rejected: cluster size 1 (PANTHENOL only); no glycerin in the formula
smoothing rejected: no dry-surface film architecture
detangling rejected: baseline slip, section 6 rule 1 (the rich R1+R4 base is one M1 observation)
secondaryFocus.derivation: Section 9.5.2 secondary rule plus section 6 G3 rule 1.
thresholdReasoning: Why zero secondaries: the emollient richness that most characterises this product has no vocabulary value, and every available proxy for it would double-count the primary M1 film.
limitations: An empty secondary set understates a six-lipid architecture; that is a vocabulary limitation, not a product finding.

hairThicknessFit.evidenceScope: Deterministic derivation from weight_potential; desired-finish/dosage prior.
hairThicknessFit.rationale: weight_potential: high maps to normal + coarse under the section 9.6 table. E2 ceiling inherited.
evidenceSignals: weight_potential = high (moderate confidence)
thresholdReasoning: Why not fine+normal+coarse: keyed to weight_potential moderate; the base-plus-alternative anchor is satisfied so moderate does not apply.
Why not fine+normal: keyed to weight_potential low, falsified on all three legs.
counterSignals: The product's own leave-in modes suggest it is usable on hair types this row excludes - a soft preference, never a rule
limitations: Inherits the weight_potential tension with the leave-in modes; if that resolved weight to moderate, this field would become fine + normal + coarse.

damageFit.evidenceScope: Deterministic derivation from conditioning_level plus the specialist-route test; broad product prior, not a repair-efficacy claim.
damageFit.rationale: conditioning_level: high with a qualifying specialist route (a distinct protein/peptide fibre-film route, i.e. repair_support_level >= medium) maps to exactly moderately_damaged + highly_damaged. The specialist result replaces the general-high set. E2 ceiling inherited.
evidenceSignals: conditioning_level = high
Qualifying specialist route (a): repair_support_level = medium via the two-species R5 route
bond_route = none, so route (b) is absent; routes (c) and (d) are absent
damageFit.derivation: Section 9.7 table row 'high with a qualifying specialist route'.
thresholdReasoning: Why not healthy + moderately_damaged: that row applies to conditioning_level high WITHOUT a qualifying specialist route; route (a) is present.
Why not all three values: the specialist result replaces the general-high set; all three are never emitted.

This is the leak the section 9.7 mask delta warns about, and it is worth flagging: an almond-milk nourishing 3in1 reaches the highly_damaged bucket entirely through a two-species protein route. If several such products do this across the first set, the delta says that is evidence the specialist test is leaking, not that drugstore masks repair hair.
counterSignals: The protein route carries no MW information and therefore no strength or breakage evidence
limitations: specialist_damage_fit trigger fired for human verification.
This value is doubly derived (from conditioning_level and repair_support_level), so it inherits both fields' uncertainty; watch-list item 1 applies.

textureFit.evidenceScope: Deterministic derivation from weight_potential plus a slip-route check; research-only.
textureFit.rationale: weight_potential: high with a coherent R1 high-slip route maps to wavy + curly + coily. E2 ceiling inherited.
evidenceSignals: weight_potential = high
Coherent R1 slip route above the tail: BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (5) + STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE (13) on a rank-2 cetearyl network
No R3 cationic polymer in the list
thresholdReasoning: Why not straight+wavy+curly: keyed to weight_potential moderate.
Why not straight+wavy: keyed to weight_potential low.
The R1/R3 disjunction is read as satisfied by R1 alone.

assumptionNotes: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN treated as a plainly qualifying R5 hydrolyzed protein although not named verbatim in the lexicon's family-5a alias list.

LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN counted as a qualifying R5 cationised protein derivative (the R5 candidate list names quaternized protein derivatives explicitly) and deliberately NOT counted toward S1 or the weight base as a cationic surfactant - the lexicon keeps those families separate.
DICAPRYLYL ETHER and COCOCAPRYLATE counted as light emollients (R4a) for S3; neither was counted as heavy for the weight anchor.
CITRIC ACID (15) read as pH/amidoamine-neutraliser context per lexicon C3, not as an active and never as bond evidence.

The weight-potential/leave-in-mode tension was recorded as a counter-signal rather than used to trigger the section 9.2 conflict fallback, because the fallback is written for exact-product positioning and this is a directions fact that G2 bars from crossing into a comparison property.

Review triggers I would fire: protein_payload_review (D4); specialist_damage_fit (damage_fit resolved to the specialist pair). No bond_claim_review (no bond positioning, no token). No tail_marker_anomaly.
No claims summary supplied. No claim-permitted leg was live; the product-name protein positioning would only have corroborated a route the formula already carried.
